label: no
controls_available: Mouse wheel on the XY, XZ, and YZ slice canvases changes the linked x/y/z focus.
Dragging empty mesh glass with the mouse orbits and tilts the reconstruction.
Dragging from one visible mesh node to another adds a mesh-node merge.
Clicking the red or green seed control and then a visible slice node places a split seed; CUT BETWEEN SEEDS removes the seeded connection.
CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH submits the final transcript; it is administrative. The full surface does not expose the simplified selectors or orbit buttons.
autonomous_processes: None during active repair: the generated nodes, edges, focus, seeds, camera, and rendered views remain unchanged between input events; no task timer, animation, physics tick, or input-independent state transition is implemented.

After certification, the asynchronous /result response can display PASS or rerender a failed specimen, but that response is triggered by the administrative action and is not an autonomous repair-phase process.
grouped_control_modes: D_merge: all full-surface mesh-node drags that add one missing connection across seeds, rounds, and attempts; outcome-affecting.
D_split: all full-surface red/green slice-seed placements followed by CUT BETWEEN SEEDS to remove one false connection across seeds, rounds, and attempts; outcome-affecting.
Linked-slice scrolling and empty-glass orbit dragging are view-only inspection modes, not outcome-affecting D candidates.
Certification is an administrative submission mode, not an outcome-affecting D candidate.

clause_i.reason: For a candidate repair mode, an observation-free policy cannot generally choose the correct opaque node pair across generated seeds from only its own prior actions and task times: the generator changes the seeded 3D geometry, target fibre, missing edges, and false edge while public identifiers do not encode fibre membership or position. This is static visual grounding, however, not dependence on an autonomous temporal process.

clause_ii.reason: At a repair point where the relevant nodes are visible, the current screenshot of the linked slices and mesh can guide the normal UI action, so a zero-width current observation can be sufficient for that static decision. It contains no changing visual trace and therefore cannot provide the required prediction of a delayed state.

clause_iii.reason: No Delta > 0 and 0 < tau < Delta can satisfy this clause. The generator creates the node positions and initial topology before play; the browser changes focus, camera, edges, and seeds only inside explicit input handlers; and the grader replays those event-driven mutations from a fixed initial state. With no autonomous task-state evolution, waiting leaves the action value and action advantage unchanged, so no useful repair opportunity becomes unavailable or strictly less effective.

common_visible_process: None. The linked planes and reconstruction are redraws of a fixed seeded specimen, and the regenerated topology is synchronously redrawn after a user merge or split. Because no visible autonomous process changes the specimen during a delay, the observation conditions above cannot be combined with clause (iii) under one D, Delta, and bounded window.

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase in this configuration: success requires explicit merge and split edits followed by administrative certification. A pre-run rate is therefore not defined; clause (iii) already fails, so the threshold cannot change the mathematical No label.

source_evidence.claim: The supplied difficulty-3 profile is three fibres, eight segments per fibre, two missing joins, one false join, ten slice positions, and crossing density 0.58.

The full interaction profile uses linked-plane scrolling, mesh orbit by drag, mesh-node merge by drag, and slice-node seeds; its configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame and a 180-second play allowance.

The shared loader validates controlled difficulty and interaction conditions and dispatches the branch_repair mechanic to its generator; the assigned control condition is not the seed fixture's historical default.
Generation is seeded and constructs fixed node coordinates, true edges, missing edges, false edges, and initial edges before returning the challenge; no task-time evolution is generated.
The public state contains fixed views, focus, slice contract, requirements, nodes, and initial edges; the hidden truth is used for grading, and the returned state has no autonomous clock or phase.
Rendering initializes a fixed edge set, focus, camera, and event model; slice changes and post-edit inspections occur only when the handler receives an input event.

Orbit, merge, seed, cut, certification, mesh dragging, slice scrolling, and slice seeding are all bound to explicit button, pointer, wheel, or click handlers; the complete implementation contains no timer, animation, or physics update loop.
The relevant CSS provides static canvas layout, cursors, hidden simplified controls, and buttons; it defines no CSS animation or transition that could change task state autonomously.
The grader starts replay from public initial edges, ground-truth edge sets, initial focus, and a fixed camera, with no elapsed-time input.

The grader changes focus, camera, topology, inspections, and seeds only while replaying submitted slice, orbit, merge, seed, split, and submit events; certification must be final and each topology edit must be followed by an inspection.
The task verifier only loads the exported result and calls the branch replay grader; it has no task-time or autonomous-state check.

The UI solver explicitly scrolls and orbits, performs each merge and false-join cut, inspects after edits, and then certifies; its short wait_for_timeout calls are test synchronization after input, not source-defined task evolution.
The runner uses observation_window_ms 0, one frame per observation, synchronous execution, and a 160 ms step cycle; the mechanic source still has no autonomous state change during that cycle.
